sources.title: Brindlewood launches Lanes API for regional carriers
Moving our routing services to Python and PostgreSQL

company_claims.text: Brindlewood builds dispatch and routing software for regional freight carriers in the US Midwest.
Brindlewood launched the Lanes API in March 2026 so carriers' dispatch systems can request optimized multi-stop routes.
Brindlewood's engineering team moved its routing services to Python and FastAPI on PostgreSQL, deployed on Kubernetes.
The Routing role builds and maintains Lanes API endpoints and writes SQL against PostgreSQL route data.
The team is likely hiring to support Lanes API adoption after the launch.
Brindlewood Freight Labs was founded in 2023, raised a seed round in January 2026 and is a team of 18, including 7 engineers.
Brindlewood is hiring its first junior engineers this year to grow the Routing team.

company_profile.note: first junior hires: the risk to reduce is ramp-up time on the routing stack

paragraphs.text: I am applying for the Junior Software Engineer role on the Routing team at Brindlewood Freight Labs. Since the Lanes API launched in March 2026, carriers' dispatch systems can request multi-stop routes from Brindlewood, and the posting describes building and maintaining those endpoints. Route planning is the problem I chose for my capstone, and I would like to keep working on it with a team that runs routing in production.

My strongest evidence is RouteWise, a route planner I built with two classmates for the volunteer drivers of the Northbridge Community Pantry. I owned the backend: a FastAPI service over a PostgreSQL schema for stops, drivers and routes, the heuristic that batches stops into routes, and the pytest tests for its endpoints. During a three-week pilot, four coordinators used it and reported that planning a shift took about 10 minutes instead of about 25. Your engineering blog describes routing services built with Python and FastAPI on PostgreSQL. If I join as one of your first junior engineers, I would start in a stack I have already used end to end.

SQL is also familiar ground. As a teaching assistant for Introduction to Databases, I held weekly office hours and graded SQL assignments, and at the Northbridge Public Library I automated a weekly reservation report with a Python script.

I want to be direct about one gap: I have not deployed services on Kubernetes. I have used Docker only for local development on RouteWise, so learning your deployment workflow would be one of my first goals, with code review from the team.
If the Routing team is now focused on helping more carriers adopt the Lanes API, I could contribute tested endpoints from my first weeks. I would welcome a conversation about the team's priorities.

interview.question: Walk us through the RouteWise batching heuristic.
interview.talking_points: Problem, constraints, how stops are grouped, what the pilot showed, what I would change.

interview.question: You have not used Kubernetes. How would you ramp up?
interview.talking_points: Honest gap; Docker locally; plan to learn the team's deployment workflow with code review.
